place: Atlanta, Georgia -- the Publix heartland of the Peach State

city_center.name: Midtown Atlanta (West Peachtree corridor)
city_center.landmark: Publix Super Market at The Plaza Midtown, 950 W Peachtree St NW; Piedmont Park, the Atlanta BeltLine, and the Fox Theatre nearby
city_center.notes: Publix Plaza Midtown is the metro anchor channel (open daily 6:45AM-10PM). Midtown is the dense residential-and-office core along the West Peachtree corridor, walkable to Piedmont Park and the BeltLine. The Sandersville frontier sister has been split into its own dedicated record -- see regions/sandersville.json (market_code US-SE-SANDERSVILLE). sources: retailer-frontier-pairs.json (Publix Plaza Midtown address/hours); en.wikipedia.org Midtown Atlanta.

featured_frontier.hook: Georgia peach + toasted pecan praline over Power Cakes at Midtown Publix, Sweet Auburn brick and Piedmont Park pine behind -- the Peach State's brunch-heartland stack
featured_frontier.photo_cue: Kodiak stack on a Midtown counter, Georgia peach compote and pecan praline drizzle, red-brick storefront and Georgia pine, BeltLine morning light; Sweet Auburn heritage-district brick as an alternate backdrop
featured_frontier.signature_ingredient: Georgia peaches (May-Aug peak Jul) + Georgia pecans (Oct-Dec peak Nov); muscadine grapes (Aug-Sep); Georgia figs (late summer)

cultural_notes: Southern brunch and biscuit culture anchor the breakfast occasion; Publix is the dominant regional grocer and a genuine cultural fixture across Georgia and the Southeast (source: Publix regional footprint; localization-table-seed.json retailer=Publix,Target)

Georgia is 'the Peach State' and a top-three US pecan producer; peaches peak in July, muscadine (the native Southern grape) Aug-Sep, and pecans at the November harvest (source: UGA extension crop calendar framing; retailer-frontier-pairs.json monthly_ingredient_notes)

Sweet Auburn (Auburn Avenue) is the historic heart of Black Atlanta business and civic life and the birthplace of the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. -- referenced respectfully as a heritage district, never as a styling prop (source: en.wikipedia.org Sweet Auburn; nps.gov MLK National Historical Park)

the Atlanta BeltLine and Ponce City Market reflect a rail-corridor-to-food-hall adaptive reuse pattern that shapes the modern metro brunch scene (source: en.wikipedia.org Atlanta BeltLine; Ponce City Market)

post-1864-fire Atlanta retains almost no antebellum fabric; its architecture reads as red-brick commercial plus modern and contemporary glass-and-steel towers (source: Architecture of Atlanta, en.wikipedia.org)

Buford Highway is one of the most concentrated immigrant food corridors in the US -- Korean, Vietnamese, Latino, and Chinese communities anchor a deep pan-Asian and Latin American food culture in the metro (source: en.wikipedia.org Buford Highway; general food-culture framing)

the metro's Piedmont setting -- red-clay soil, Georgia pine, rolling terrain -- is the recurring natural backdrop even inside the city (source: en.wikipedia.org Piedmont (United States); Ultisol soil color)

building_materials: adaptive-reuse rail-corridor steel (BeltLine / Ponce City Market)
landscape_motifs: Georgia pine and pecan-orchard rows on the metro edge
design_palette._provenance_note: red-clay ochre grounded in Georgia Piedmont Ultisol soil color (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultisol). brick red + Georgia granite grounded in Architecture of Atlanta + Georgia stone trim (en.wikipedia.org; sah-archipedia.org). BeltLine rail-steel from the adaptive-reuse rail corridor (en.wikipedia.org Atlanta BeltLine). peach/muscadine/pecan colors from produce. hex values are perceptual approximations, not sampled -- flag for brand-fit review against the fixed Kodiak brand palette.
